**Conditions**
- **Data:** MTEB score matrices with their real missing cells (NaN), 6 subsets from 21 % to 70 % observed. `sparse_subsets.csv` lists models x tasks, density, median observed cells per model, tested models, families and organisations.
  - `eng_full`: English tasks seen by at least 20 models, 445 x 335, 21 % observed, median 60 cells per model, 337 models tested.
  - `eng_d30`, `eng_d50`, `eng_d70`: English subsets trimmed to 30, 50 and 70 % observed. Sizes are 332x295, 268x176 and 226x134, with 215-332 models tested.
  - `all_d30`, `all_d50`: all tasks, trimmed to 30 and 50 %. Sizes are 331x705 and 236x517, with median 181 and 308 cells per model.
- **Split and test models:** grouped 10-fold, held out by model family. A model is tested if it has at least 30 observed cells. Training columns need at least 10 observed training cells and are standardised on their observed cells. Identity transform only.
- **Candidates and targets:** for each tested model and each of 3 partitions, the targets T are a random 30 % of its observed cells and the candidates C are the rest of its observed cells.

- **Predictors:**

  - `pw`: pairwise-complete correlation, PSD-clipped and shrunk toward the identity.
  - `softimpute`: masked Soft-Impute fold-in.
  - `fa` and `pw` are the two best predictors that handle missing cells.
- **LOBO analogue:** all of C predicts T, using `fa` and `pw`; the reference is the lower of the two (`lobo` rows in `sparse_refs.csv`). Closure is therefore not capped at 1.
- **Grid:** k = 1..6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20. There is no k=30, because C holds at most 70 % of a model's 30-100 observed cells.

The six subsets keep the real missing cells of the MTEB score matrix. \emph{English, 21\%} holds the 445 models and 335 English tasks reported for at least 20 models (a median of 60 observed cells per model; 337 models have at least 30). The other subsets are greedy trimmings of the English tasks (332$\times$295, 268$\times$176 and 226$\times$134 at 30, 50 and 70\% observed) and of all tasks (331$\times$705 and 236$\times$517 at 30 and 50\%); the trimmed subsets are one greedy choice among many. \paragraph{Cheaper evaluation of one benchmark.}
Anchor points \citep{vivek2024anchor}, efficient benchmarking \citep{perlitz2024efficient}, tinyBenchmarks \citep{polo2024tiny}, metabench \citep{kipnis2024metabench} and IRT-based adaptive item selection \citep{fluid2025} reduce the number of \emph{items} needed to estimate a model's score on one benchmark. We choose whole benchmarks, and the target is the score on \emph{other} benchmarks.

\paragraph{Cross-benchmark predictability.}
A few capability components computed from many models predict downstream scores \citep{ruan2024observational}, and skill-level scaling laws transfer across families \citep{polo2024sloth}; \citet{perlitz2024benchbench} show that conclusions about benchmark agreement depend on protocol choices. \paragraph{Matrix completion.}

Cold-start item selection in recommenders \citep{elahi2016active}, column subset selection \citep{mahoney2009cur} and sensor placement \citep{krause2005sensors,ranieri2014framesense} choose which entries to observe, and greedy selection for linear prediction has guarantees through the submodularity ratio \citep{das2011submodular,bian2017greedy}. shown.message:
The sparse-matrix write-up is pushed to `dev`. The main text now has an undefined `Table~\ref{tab:sparse}` until `figtab-repo` delivers the table, so `internal-review-repo`'s M1 is not yet answered. I'm ending the turn until `figtab-repo` and `experiment-repo` reply.

- **Results used:** the six sparse MTEB subsets from `experiment-repo`, 21–70% of cells observed.
- **Main text:** a new Section 6.6, "A leaderboard with missing cells".
  - Greedy selection beats random at every k from 1 to 20 on every subset, for both predictors. The interval excludes zero except for the pairwise predictor (pw) at k=20 on the 21% subset.
  - At k=3 the gap to random is 5–7% of the random error with pw and 6–24% with the factor model.
  - At k=3 greedy selection closes 0.71–0.80 of the gap to the leave-one-benchmark-out predictor (pw), against 0.55–0.74 for random.
- **Stated limits:** identity transform only, nothing below 21% observed, models with fewer than 30 observed cells are not tested, and k stops at 20.
- **Appendix and the rest:** a new Appendix subsection describes the sparse protocol. The abstract and contribution (iii) now include the sparse result. The abstract also defines A-optimal in a clause and says the 10% margin is met on one pool of three. The Limitations paragraph is updated to match.
- **Moves for space:** the main text had no spare page, so Fig. 5 (the closed-form risk) and the history-sweep paragraph moved to the appendix. The text keeps the numbers and cites them as "Appendix Figure".
- **Main-text length:** the main text ends on page 9 with about 98 pt of slack, but the new table needs about 170 pt. I'll trim about seven more lines once I see its real height.
- **`figtab-repo`#6:** I asked them for the main-text table (one row per subset) and an appendix figure and table, with that height budget.
- **`experiment-repo`#7:** I asked them to confirm how the text describes the computed sparse numbers.

After both land, I'll pull `dev`, fix the fit, and cut a new candidate toward `final`.
